question.text: This grandnephew of Julius Caesar was the first emperor and founder of the Roman Empire, and outlasted the Second Triumvirate.
question.clue: This ruler reportedly shouted at Quintilius Varus to "give me back my legions" after his forces lost the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.

swap.leadin: China wasn't the only country that built great walls.
swap.text: This Roman emperor built a namesake wall to mark the northern boundary of Roman Britain. He also suppressed the Bar Kokhba revolt in Judea.
swap.clue: In his youth, this character receives the "bloody aspersion" from a cult he forbids after the initiation of his twenty-year-old lover, whose suicide is presaged when they watch a sacrificial victim struck by lightning with his physician Hermogenes.

question.text: The grandest examples of gladiatorial combat took place in this Roman arena, the largest amphitheater ever built.
question.clue: While not for getting sick, this location's vomitorium allowed for the rapid entrance and exits of spectators to various parts of it.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about ancient Roman attire.
swap.text: This type of robe was often worn by senators. Usually woven from white wool, it was draped over the shoulder and wrapped around the body.
swap.clue: During a triumph, the celebrated general used the picta version of this traditional Roman object.

question.leadin: The dictator Quintus Fabius Maximus' delaying tactics in this war earned him the epithet Cunctator (kuhngk-TEY-ter), leading him to be replaced by the consuls Varro and Paullus.
question.text: Name this war, in which the Romans suffered an envelopment by Carthaginian forces at the Battle of Cannae (kan-AY). In another battle in this war, Scipio (SKIP-ee-oh) Africanus crushed Carthage at the Battle of Zama.
question.clue: This war began with an attack on the city of Saguntum, and its eventual victors suffered terrible defeats at Trebia and Lake Trasimene.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the pincer movement, in which separated forces attack the enemy from both flanks at once.
swap.text: Hannibal Barca executed a pincer during this battle of the Second Punic War, inflicting heavy casualties on the forces of Aemilius Paulus and Terrentius Varro. This battle resulted in the formal adoption of the Fabian strategy.
swap.clue: Eight legions - the most then assembled - took part in this clash, an obsession of von Schlieffen, which led to the principes being deployed farther behind the hastati and the permanent adoption of the strategy of Fabius Cunctator.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of Rome.
question.text: Rome's first king and legendary founder was this man. This man murdered his twin brother, Remus.
question.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

swap.leadin: This woman's revolt occurred after the death of her husband Prasutagus and the rape of her two daughters.
swap.text: Name this Iceni queen who revolted against the Roman Empire. She either died from sickness or via suicide after the failure of the revolt.
swap.clue: This person succeeded Prasutagus as the leader of the Iceni tribe and may have been inspired by to act by her public flogging and the rape of her daughters.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people who may have come from Lydia or Umbria.
question.text: This Italian civilization, which was eventually absorbed by the Romans, had no centralized government. Instead, it was comprised of a loose Confederation of cities like Clusium and Veii.
question.clue: The names of gods in this language are on a sheep liver-shaped bronze artifact used for haruspicy found at Piacenza.

swap.leadin: Name these women who bedeviled the Roman Empire.
swap.text: When this woman's husband Prasutagus died, Rome annexed his former kingdom, prompting this queen of the Iceni to lead a revolt in East Anglia that was put down by Paulinus.
swap.clue: This person's popularity as a patriotic symbol in Victorian Britain was influenced by the theory that her name comes from a root meaning "victory" in Celtic.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the lives of women in the Roman world.
question.text: One important religious position held exclusively by women was this group of female priests. They were held to be incorruptible, and tended to the sacred fire of the goddess of the hearth.
question.clue: Livy claimed that a traitorous member of this group was crushed by the shields of the Sabines and then thrown from the namesake Tarpeian Rock.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the early years of the Byzantine empire.
swap.text: Two advisors to Constantine had this name. The one from Caesarea wrote histories like the Chronicon.
swap.clue: The man who baptized Constantine had this name. A more famous Roman with this name was a Bishop of Caesarea who wrote an Ecclesiastical History of the early church.

question.text: Before fleeing to the Balearics, Mago was defeated at this battle near Seville by a concealed force of Romans under Scipio Africanus. The battle of Baecula and this battle ended Carthaginian power in Spain.
question.clue: This battle's victor unusually placed legions on the wings and auxiliaries in the centre, later creating a concave formation that mirrored a battle occurring ten years prior.

swap.leadin: Decabalus was the last independent leader of this region.
swap.text: Name this region that was conquered by Trajan, which he depicted in his column. It had its capital at Sarmizegetusa.
swap.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

question.leadin: In a poem describing God, he wrote that God "is indescribable" even to Jesus.
question.text: Name this author of "Thalia" whose views were criticized by Athanasius (ath-uh-NAY-shus) in On the Councils of Ariminum and Seleucia (uh-RIM-in-um and si-LOO-shuh)
question.clue: While speaking at an event, this person was apocryphally slapped by an outraged man from Patara.

swap.text: Earlier, the defensive Multangular Tower was built along the Roman walls of this city. This city, the capital of Britannia Inferior, was where Constantine I was proclaimed emperor.

question.leadin: One part of this structure lends its name to the Vindolanda Tablets discovered in the 1970s.
question.text: Identify this structure whose archaeological remains can be found at sites like Brocolitia and Cilurnum.
question.clue: A birthday invitation was found on one of the Vindolanda tablets, which were unearthed near this structure.

swap.text: Name this speech which was written to acquit its title politician of the murder of Clodius.
swap.clue: This defense oration which becamse known in published form, composed for the Optimate rival of Julius Caesar, who was charged with murder following an incident at Bovillae.

question.leadin: A scholar of ancient Rome employed her expertise in this non-history-related profession to determine that classicists had been mistranslating the word "acus" ("AY-cuss").
question.text: Name this profession of Janet Stephens, who analyzed texts such as an epigram by Martial in which an enslaved woman with this profession named Plecusa is killed. Members of this profession used tools like vittae ("VIT-tee") and calamistra.
question.answerHtml: hairdressers [or hairstylists; or ornatrix; or ornatrices; prompt on stylists or salon workers or beauticians or people who cut hair; reject “barbers” or “maids” or “domestic workers”] {Acus is a catch-all term for several different tools, but in this context refers to a sewing needle used for weaving hair. Vittae are hair ribbons. Calamistra are curling irons.}

swap.leadin: Answer the following about banditry in the Roman empire.
swap.text: This late Roman thinker tried to work out what differentiates a kingdom from a "bandit community," or latrocinium, such as Spartacus's rebels, in his book The City of God.
swap.clue: This Doctor of the Church who was converted from Manichaeism to Catholicism through the prayers of his mother, St. Monica. His works include City of God and Confessions.
